purpose: Collect one new paired calibration from a visible-light webcam and an oblique Hikvision IR stream, using pre-click windows, total numerical fusion and scalar pupil/glint diagnostics.

activities.label: implement paired webcam and Hikvision calibration with click-closing pre-click windows
add a lightweight scalar pupil/glint branch to the Hikvision path without a second GPU model or raw-frame persistence
verify total numeric output, grouped target validation and non-persistence policy offline
verify synthetic pupil/glint recovery, scalar-only serialization and separation from the screen mapper

queries.expression: does one paired point produce independent webcam and Hikvision summaries from samples collected before the click
does the dual eye-centre proxy return a numerical estimate with two sensors, one sensor or no current sensor window without claiming screen gaze or metric depth

assumptions: The same six feature vector and ten design terms remain compatible with the existing VIZZ profile.
The pinned RetinaFace, screen-gaze and MobileOne ONNX assets are available locally and can initialize through CUDA.
The two camera streams can be read in one Python process with a bounded timestamp skew.
The Hikvision stream is processed night video; RTSP exposes encoded video rather than a sensor-plane IR measurement.
The pupil/glint detector is a conservative diagnostic heuristic and can confuse eyelashes, reflections or exposure boundaries with optical features.
Metric stereo triangulation is deferred until camera intrinsics and relative extrinsics are measured.
kill_tests: The runtime must not start sampling after the click.
The runtime must not persist raw frames or credentials.
The grouped validation must not split consecutive frames into independent folds.
The fusion must return a numeric screen coordinate for zero, one or two available sensors.
The runtime must use both new sensor calibrations rather than silently reusing the prior profile.
The IR branch must remain separate from the mapper until a held-out comparison proves useful signal beyond exposure and camera geometry.
unknowns: Whether the oblique Hikvision eye-centre proxy is stable enough for a metric stereo solve.
Whether the two streams can maintain acceptable skew on the current 10 Mbps negotiated link.
Whether a physical stereo-board stage will be needed for reliable K/R/t recovery.
Whether pupil/glint candidates remain stable across the real Hikvision stream, pose and illumination.
The first human capture predates polarity and MAD aggregation, so those diagnostics must be collected on the next run.
